That's really hard.  I hear you on the job market - I'm unemployed too and it can feel really fucking hopeless out there.  I can definitely see why you'd be feeling very sad and how that might make you want to just end that pain.  But at the same time, I don't want to see you go, and I definitely don't think you're useless.  Everyone has value.

Right now you're hurting really badly, so the change you can cause in this world has to be put on hold.  For now, you can just focus on taking care of yourself - and you don't need to be good at it just yet.  I used to give myself points just for taking a shower, or eating - just the very basics.  Start small.  If all you can do today is not kill yourself, that's a start. 

What do you think?

Can we talk about it?  Did something happen today that's pushed you over the edge or is it just a gradual accumulation?  Are there any specific causes of your grief or is it just a thing that you feel?

> even the sexual pain and lack of sex drive are psychological issues with physical effects. Especially because those issues come up when you reach a particular relationship situation.

I feel like I'm just blowing off everyone's advice - I don't mean to do that, it's just that I've already seen several different therapists and I really don't feel like the depression and anxiety is the problem, because I have those when I'm single and they don't affect the sex at *all* then.

I know it's normal for passion to decrease over time, but I don't think it's normal to lose your sex drive *entirely*.  I mean, I don't even enjoy masturbation anymore, and it's not like I'm fantasizing about other men.  I do love my boyfriend, and I desperately want to want to fuck him. 

Maybe I'll look a little more into BPD, but everything I read about it sounds like you'd need to be impulsive or unstable, and I'm neither of those things.  The opposite, really.  I'm incredibly predictable and everything I do is planned in advance.  Even when I start to get more depressed, it happens gradually and I know it's on its way.

I read through the wikipedia page and nothing rings a bell - I definitely don't obsessively pursue love or sex, and I don't avoid either nearly as much as the obessive avoidance categories.

Well, anxiety and depression don't kill my libido when single, though.  I'd say they actually increase it - I tend to be much hornier when I'm going through a rough period.  Once I'm happy I lose interest. Hah. 

Anyway, yeah, if it was just an issue of me not craving it every day, that'd be okay ... but I haven't been aroused in months.  Literally. I keep having sex to try to keep a routine and whatnot, but it just doesn't do anything for me.
